summary: This bill amends 18 U.S.C. § 111 to create new 20-year felony penalties for using a vehicle to forcibly interfere with DHS or DOJ officers on duty and for forcibly interfering with such officers while they are inside a federal law enforcement vehicle.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill does not address taxes, tax policy, or revenue measures.
No connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
The bill makes no reference to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill enhances penalties for obstructing DHS and DOJ officers, which could indirectly support immigration enforcement by protecting officers involved in border or immigration functions. However, the text does not directly address immigration pathways, border policy, or enforcement priorities, making any relation tangential at best.
No provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not involve military or defense spending or policy.
No environmental or climate-related content.
The bill has no bearing on welfare programs or social safety net policies.
Unrelated to education policy or funding.
No mention of drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement of drug laws.

The bill directly amends federal criminal law (18 U.S.C. § 111) to create enhanced penalties of up to 20 years imprisonment for forcibly interfering with DHS or DOJ officers, including through use of a vehicle or while officers are in a law enforcement vehicle. This clearly advances tougher sentencing and stronger protections for law enforcement.
